comment: Memory-API inventory for the phase-2a overlay (plan task MS1/A4). One entry per API,
recording the ROLE of each argument so a consumer writes tag lookups instead of
hard-coded argument indices. Sources: POSIX Issue 7, Linux man-pages (malloc(3),
memcpy(3), read(2), ...), and the FFmpeg usage seen while building the litmus corpus.
Deliberately omitted: wide-char and _s variants (wcscpy, memcpy_s, ...), Win32 APIs,
and alloca (stack allocation has no family in the tag vocabulary yet). They surface in
the coverage report as 'seen but not inventoried', which is how this list is meant to
grow - an entry here needs its man-page argument roles, nothing else.
Argument indices are 1-based. `untrustedCall` marks a call whose RESULT or variadic
outputs carry untrusted data with no single buffer argument to point at (getenv, the
scanf family). C++ new/delete are indistinguishable from new[]/delete[] in the graph
(frontend probe NOTES-frontend.md Q3), so both carry the plain `new` family.
Count-by-size allocators (calloc, reallocarray) declare both factors: `count` is the
element-count role and `len` the byte-size role; both arguments carry the mem-len tag
and the overflow question is asked about the product (part 4, D1). A realloc is the
third family, `realloc`: it invalidates its input pointer and returns a fresh
allocation, so it carries neither the alloc nor the free tag.

Clamp entries (part 2, MS3): the value records what the call establishes about its result - min (bounded above by each argument), max (bounded below), clip (arg2 below, arg3 above). FFMIN/FFMAX/av_clip are FFmpeg's clamping macros; a project's own MYMIN is an external-config entry in the same shape. Used by GuardPass for clamps the frontend left unexpanded.
Nullable-return entries (part 5, E3): `nullableReturn` marks an API whose result may be NULL
for reasons other than allocation failure - the strchr/strstr family returning no-match NULL.
Allocation-family calls (alloc/realloc) are nullable BY DEFINITION and need no flag. The pass
emits `nullable-return` on the call for MS-NULL-001: a dereference of the result with no
narrowing guard between the call and the use.
